# Study 9.8 — Minimum-wage increases of 2019–2024 by state and activity: generated results

*Generated by `empirics/code/enoe/minimum_wage_bite/04_report.py`; do not edit by hand. Cells: 31 units (Mexico City and the State of Mexico combined) × 20 activity groups, non-oil, with at least 100 full-time wage employees with reported income in 2018. Treatment: 2018 bite (share of those workers below the 2019 minimum). Model: cell, state × year and activity × year effects; weights 2018 employment; clustered by state. Coefficients are per unit of bite (0 to 1). Post estimand: mean of the 2022–2024 coefficients, relative to 2018.*

## 1. Treatment

Cells: 479. Bite: mean 0.115, median 0.078, interquartile range 0.037 to 0.159, maximum 0.716. Correlation with the 2017 bite 0.93, with the Kaitz index 0.69, with the formal-only bite 0.74.

## 6. Implied effect on state productivity relative to the least-exposed cells (illustration)

Combining the post estimates for employment and value added per worker, the implied effect on state non-oil productivity, relative to a counterfactual in which every cell behaved like a cell with zero bite, has a median across units of 2.06 log points and ranges from 0.36 to 6.49.
